summary:
# NOTES: "American Boys Afloat; or, Cruising in the Orient" by Oliver Optic (William T. Adams), Lee & Shepard, Boston, 1893. Gutenberg #75149. Fifth vol. of "All-Over-the-World" series. Single book.

## FRONT MATTER
- Dedicated "To my excellent friend Dr. William P. Leavitt, one of my fellow-travellers in foreign lands."
- Preface: continuation of Louis Belgrave and Felix McGavonty; reinforced by Morris Woolridge and Scott Fencelowe ("The Big Four"). Steam-yacht Salihé found at Gibraltar, renamed Maud, becomes tender of Guardian-Mother. Voyage Gibraltar→Constantinople "cruising in the Orient." Dated Dorchester, Mass., Aug 15, 1893.
- Chapter list: I Salihé Alongside; II Big Four Arrange Excursion; III Possible Dangers; IV Exploration of Gibraltar Bay; V Mouth of Palmones River; VI Battle on Deck of Salihé; VII Prisoners in Cabin; VIII Moral Conspiracy; IX Working Up Details; X Lassoing the Scotchman; XI Return of Victorious Knight-Errant; XII Smugglers Make Trip to Algeciras; XIII What Is Worth Knowing About Gibraltar; XIV American Witnesses in Spanish Court; XV Exploring Rock; XVI Addition for Fun of Big Four; XVII Ship's Company of Steamer Maud; XVIII Afternoon Excursion to Tangier; XIX Enter Ali-Noury Pacha and Fatimé; XX Unexpected Peril; XXI Euchring Grand Mogul; XXII Consternation on Board; XXIII Fugitive from Enemy; XXIV Stormy Interview with Ali-Noury; XXV Starboard and Port Watches; XXVI Pacha Caught a Tartar; XXVII Lessons in Navigation; XXVIII Morris on Rule of Road; XXIX Water-Famine; XXX Maud Inclined to Turn Somersets; XXXI Captain Scott Sets Reefed Foresail; XXXII Meeting of Two Steamers; XXXIII Professor's Lecture on Algeria; XXXIV Oriental Views in Algiers; XXXV Arrival at Constantinople; XXXVI City of Sultan; XXXVII Sultan and Dancing Dervishes; XXXVIII His Highness in Oriental City.

## CHARACTERS
- Louis Belgrave: 17 (millionaire at 16), owner of Guardian-Mother; "Sir Louis" (Uncle Moses' nickname, knight-errant); mother Mrs. Belgrave (nervous, cured by Dr. Hawkes). Lives Von Blonk Park, NJ. Studies with Professor Pierre Giroud. Never drinks.
- Felix McGavonty: Irish-American, Milesian, dialect varies ("Oi", "moighty", "my darlint"); captain's clerk; father "disappeared," mother dead. Has revolver.
- George Scott Fencelowe ("Scott", "middy"): 18, reformed; adopted son of bank defaulter; was in Pacha's service; expert with saw and lasso; later Captain Scott of Maud; promoted to cabin, stateroom No. 14.
- Morris Woolridge: 14, youngest; son of Lowell Woolridge (Fifth Ave millionaire, yacht Blanche); pilot/first officer/mate of Maud; revolver bought in London.
- Felipe (Philip) Garcias: 18 Spanish engineer of Salihé; fled Pacha at Mogadore; devout Catholic; later engineer of Maud; fears Pacha.
- Captain Royal Ringgold: commander of Guardian-Mother; ex-navy; calls boys "Big Four"; calls Louis "Sir Louis."
- Uncle Moses (Squire Moses Scarburn): trustee, lawyer, 226 lbs; humorous. Dr. Philip Hawkes: physician, 226 lbs. Professor Pierre Giroud: French scholar. Mrs. Blossom: housekeeper/companion.
- Mr. Lowell & Mrs. Woolridge; Blanche Woolridge: 16, beautiful, Pacha's object of desire.
- Mr. Melancthon Sage: chief steward; Monsieur Odervie: chief cook. Mr. Boulong: first officer; Mr. Gaskette: second officer (speaks Spanish); Mr. Shafter: chief engineer; Mr. Sentrick; Sparks, Bangs, Twist, Stevens, Pitts (cook/steward of Maud), Knott, Williams (seamen), Don / John Donald (fugitive English oiler, fourth engineer of Spanish steamer Guadiana; later second engineer of Maud).
- Captain W. Penn Sharp & Mrs. Sharp: Viking; Sergeant Files.
- Giles Chickworth: owner of Salihé (bought from Pacha for £100), chairman of a society; engineer also Spanish-speaking; charges 5s/hour. Sold steamer to Louis for £? (paid 30 shillings then bought steamer for ~£100/$500).
- Gray: Scotch smuggler (Scottish, speaks English), leader of gang; Diego Velazquez (Captain, schooner Golondrina), Lucio, Francisco (wheelman, knife), Pedro (engineer watchman).
- Ali-Noury Pacha (Grand Mogul): Moroccan, from Mogadore; steam-yacht Fatimé (~400 tons); educated St. Cyr; pursues Blanche.
- Judge Salazar: 75, bachelor, at Algeciras court.
- Macias: guide at Gibraltar. Dimitri (Greek guide), Munif (Turkish guide) at Constantinople.

## BOOK EVENTS (in order)
1. Ch I: Gibraltar New Mole. Big four spot Salihé (now black). Felipe identifies her. Pilot Giles Chickworth. Captain Ringgold; Sharp of Viking.
2. Ch II: Chickworth hires Salihé for evening, 6 pm, 5s/hour; Louis is owner; Felix "Mr. Chairman" banter; Ringgold approves.
3. Ch III: Felipe as engineer; Scott pilot; Chickworth set ashore at Ragged Staff. Green light at landing; Verde Island light; Carbonera Mountain (971 ft); San Roque; Point Mala; Palmones River; Point Mirador; Rinconcillo; Old Mole; Neutral Ground; San Felipe.
4. Ch IV: Louis/Felix cosmography talk; Columbus. Five men in boat approach.
5. Ch V: Salihé grounds on bar at mouth of Palmones. Boat with Diego (Spaniard, "Board her, Gray!") and Gray. Gray offers money (£2, £3, £4, £20); Louis refuses. Golondrina (swallow) schooner in river. Gray whistles; Felix cuts painter.
6. Ch VI: Gray boards with four men; Scott cuts heaveline with hatchet; fights with hand-saw; Gray swings spare tiller. Prisoners tied.
7. Ch VII: Morris at wheel overthrown by Diego. Prisoners locked in cabin. Plan of resistance. Scott's saw dropped out window.
8. Ch VIII: Moral conspiracy; overheard plan; Golondrina to be towed; Diego goes on schooner, Lucio on board. Felix and Louis cut bonds with knife in vest pocket.
9. Ch IX: Scott's lasso plan. Morris goes out window, unlocks door (cold potato wager). Lasso made from heaveline. Gray told "Dutchmen."
10. Ch X: Lasso on Gray at standing-room; Scott jumps on him; bound with belt and lanyards; Francisco subdued (knife); Pedro subdued; Felipe in engine-room. Louis fires revolver in air to scare Diego.
11. Ch XI: Louis's conversation with Gray ("Von Blonk Park, NJ"); Ringgold hails; Mr. Boulong and 10 seamen board; Velazquez and Lucio taken.
12. Ch XII: Algeciras; smugglers to police; Scott promoted to cabin; Ringgold lectures on Gibraltar (Tarik, 711; 1309 Guzman; 1704 English-Dutch capture; siege 1779-83; 1,439 ft; monkeys ~30; ~20,000 inhabitants; 5,000 troops).
13. Ch XIII: Salihé to Algeciras with witnesses; Gray, Velazquez sentenced (1 yr smuggling, 1 yr assault).
14. Ch XIV: Court testimony; judge asks if Louis drinks ("never a drop"); Mrs. Belgrave testifies.
15. Ch XV: Judge Salazar to dine; Chickworth; Ragged Staff; Macias; St. George's Hall; Signal (El Hacho); Almeda; Europa Point; Mr. Bright.
16. Ch XVI: Dinner with judge; Ringgold buys Salihé; name changed to Maud (Mrs. Belgrave's name); Scott elected captain by vote.
17. Ch XVII: Ship's company: Scott captain, Morris pilot/mate, Felipe engineer, Louis and Felix deck-hands. Maud sign carved by Chickworth's carver.
18. Ch XVIII: Excursion to Tangier, 30 miles; Scott's navigation (variation 18°50′); Felipe's speed 10.5 knots.
19. Ch XIX: Fatimé appears; Pacha claims Maud; Maud 12 knots by log; Malabata Point.
20. Ch XX: Pacha accuses Scott of theft; Fatimé chasing; Felipe terrified (15 ft draft).
21. Ch XXI: Scott runs close to shore (Almirante Rocks, Cana Coja Reef); Maud outruns Fatimé to Tarifa; Felix steering; "euchre the Grand Mogul."
22. Ch XXII: Maud reaches Gib at 6:45 pm; bolt removed from piston; Ringgold orders Boulong to stop Pacha.
23. Ch XXIII: John Donald, oiler, swims from Fatimé; hides in forecastle. Ringgold refuses Pacha.
24. Ch XXIV: Pacha's barge; gangway hauled in; Pacha dunked; Ringgold refuses ("reputation bad in Funchal"); Pacha challenges to duel. Ringgold decides to send Maud to sea with Scott and Felipe.
25. Ch XXV: Watches: Scott captain, Morris mate (port watch with Louis); starboard: Scott and Felix. Pitts cook. Navigation/watches.
26. Ch XXVI: Maud leaves at midnight; Gibraltar Pacha assault in street; Ringgold & Uncle Moses fight; Pacha fined. Maud 80 miles, Alboran.
27. Ch XXVII: Lessons in navigation, knots, statute miles; Ringgold's red crosses; Pacha's court trial.
28. Ch XXVIII: Rules of road; couplets; Morris and Louis at sea; Pitts discovers empty water-casks (leaking).
29. Ch XXIX: Water famine; Don calks casks; felucca at Alboran sells water (20 pesetas per barrel, $6 per barrel with casks, fish).
30. Ch XXX: Maud rolls; backing wind; meal times 7:30, 11:30, 5:30.
31. Ch XXXI: Gale; Scott bends reefed foresail; log 13 knots.
32. Ch XXXII: Two steamers meet; Ringgold's report; Maud continues to Constantinople.
33. Ch XXXIII: Lecture on Algeria (Professor Giroud); Algiers quarantine; Blanche visits Maud; Tunis not visited.
34. Ch XXXIV: Algiers Place Royale; Blanche, Louis talk; Cape Matapan; Blanche visits Maud.
35. Ch XXXV: Greece; Cerigo; Bosporus; arrival at Golden Horn.
36. Ch XXXVI: Turkey lecture (Abdul-Hamid II; Sultan); Rue de Pera; Dimitri & Munif guides.
37. Ch XXXVII: Sultan's procession; Dancing Dervishes; Louis & Felix spot Pacha at Misserie's Hotel.
38. Ch XXXVIII: Pacha apologizes; Ringgold refuses friendship; Fatimé in Golden Horn; Maud excursion; Constantinople two weeks; sequel: "The Young Navigators; or, The Foreign Cruise of the Maud."

## SERIES LIST (back matter)
First series: A Missing Million; A Millionaire at Sixteen; A Young Knight-Errant; Strange Sights Abroad. Second series: American Boys Afloat; The Young Navigators; Up and Down the Nile; Asiatic Breezes. Third: Across India; Half Round the World; Four Young Explorers.
